title: Heat Pump Rebates in Richmond Hill 2026: Per-Ton Rebates for Houses
desc: Richmond Hill heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: $500 per ton for gas homes, $1,250 per ton for electric, oil, propane and wood.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Richmond Hill
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Richmond Hill has 69,315 households, 78% owners and 76% living in eligible house types. The rebate is simple on paper, with several details that can trip up a quote.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Richmond Hill
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 4,310 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981 in Richmond Hill, 57% of households in detached houses and 3.7% reporting a home needing major repairs. 19% live in tall apartments, which the program excludes.

A qualifying model must be active on NRCan's list, be variable capacity with three or more speeds, have HSPF2 of at least 6.6 for Region V and SEER2 of at least 15.2, and have a rated heating capacity of at least 12,000 BTU/h at 8.3°C. Ask the contractor for the model number and check it against the list on the day you sign, because delisted models do not qualify.

A rented heat pump qualifies at $500 per ton up to $2,000 for any heating fuel, and a ground-source rental pays $3,000 flat. The signed rental agreement replaces the purchase invoice at the post-installation stage. This is a way to avoid a large upfront cost, though you should compare the rental total over the term with buying.

The program pays one rebate per home. If your home needs two or three outdoor units, they count together toward that one rebate. You cannot claim a second rebate for a second project later on the same home under this stream.

Ask three things before signing: that the company is on the Participating HVAC Contractor List, that it will file the pre-installation application and wait for written approval, and that it will file the post-installation application within 30 days. A Richmond Hill owner who has these answers in writing is protected from the most common reasons a claim fails.
claim_heading: How to claim in Richmond Hill
claim_steps: Choose a model from NRCan's list and confirm it is active.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
faq: Can I rent a heat pump?
Yes, with a rebate of $500 per ton up to $2,000.
Can I claim twice for one home?
HSPF2 6.6 for Region V and SEER2 15.2.
